body:
Thanks!

Two things:

* The spec needs to say what the accepted value space for the attribute is.
* I think we should just go ahead and define the UA processing for this at the same time. https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/110 -- if you want to take a stab, that would be great, otherwise one of the editors (or @hober?) can push more commits to this branch.
For the first thing, I was thinking the same. But how should I do it? Just add a `p` in the note?
So, how should I proceed with this? Can you guys give me a couple more hints?

At the top of `source` there's this comment you want to read:
```
 !   Adding a new attribute involves editing the following sections:
 !    - The IDL and content attributes for the relevant elements
 !    - element and attribute indexes
```
The `link` element currently doesn't have a `color` attribute, so a bunch of places will need to be modified to add it. You can look at existing attributes to see how you need to go about defining one. Where it's introduced you'll need to use the `<dfn>` element for instance.

The other thing would be to make `mask-icon` a value defined directly by the standard. You can look at other values already in the standard to see how to go about that.

The other thing we'll need is one or more tests of sorts in https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests (can be manual, but if color has some kind of parsing rules associated with it those could be automated tests).

That's all I can think of right now. Feel free to ping us on IRC by the way, I think this PR just dropped off the radar for a bit.

>> So, how should I proceed with this? Can you guys give me a couple more hints

I can’t think of anything specific to add to what @annevk already said in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/2230#issuecomment-271804158

I will personally try to be around as much as I can on #whatwg IRC for the rest of this week and next. I’m traveling and on CET time and in meetings during work hours, but can still respond to questions some then (especially if I can answer them relatively quickly). And outside of those hours also around (with more time to respond).

One thing I noticed is that WebKit does not implement a color IDL attribute, and since they are the only ones that implement this feature, probably we should follow their lead in the spec by defining only the content attribute and not the IDL attribute. It's a little unusual but such is life in meta-tag-land.

That seems like a bug -- we generally include a reflecting IDL unless there is a good reason not to. That the initial implementation doesn't have the IDL attribute doesn't seem like a good reason in itself.

@hober do you think WebKit could implement the `color` IDL attribute?

Hmm. To me it seemed like link might be a special case. My feelings are vague, but something like---it's harmless if you include `<link rel="mask-icon" color="..." href="...">` and nothing happens in non-WebKit browsers. But it's harmful if you start doing e.g. `myLinkEl.color.substring(1)` or similar in non-WebKit browsers; that will cause a JS exception. Whereas `myLinkEl.getAttribute("color").substring(1)` will work in every browser, even in non-WebKit ones where the color is ignored.

The alternative is getting every browser to implement the attribute reflection, even if they don't actually use the link element in any way. Or asking WebKit to come up with an alternate design that does not involve new attributes (e.g. `<meta name="mask-icon-color" content="...">`). Ideally we would have caught this earlier, I guess.
This seems not so different from `<link sizes>` which has IDL attribute. It should be supported even if no icon is downloaded or shown.

OK. I guess that moves this into the realm of "needs implementer interest". But for @XhmikosR's purposes, let's not worry about that, and just add the reflected attribute. I guess I'll open a new issue to discuss.

I'm now questioning whether we should actually land the processing model for this in the spec (as opposed to just allowing it, and the color attribute, in conformant documents---as the original PR here does). It doesn't have two interested implementations.

On the other hand, maybe link rels and meta values are a special case? We landed meta theme-color despite I believe only one implementation these days. (At some point WebKit supported it, but no longer I believe.)

It also seems weird to specify a `color` IDL attribute that just reflects the `color=""` content attribute and tell browsers to implement that even if they don't use mask icons. After all, if you don't do anything with `rel="preload"`, you don't implement the `as` IDL attribute. If you don't implement subresource integrity, you don't implement the `integrity` IDL attribute.

`preload` and `integrity` affect processing that is visible to the javascript, so they should be feature-checkable. I suppose it could make sense to have `color` IDL be a feature test for `mask-icon`, though...
Wait, for feature-testing `mask-icon` one should use `link.relList.supports('mask-icon')`

Same argument for `as` and `integrity` then, right? I dunno, it feels like there are three distinct features: preload, SRI, and mask-icon, which come with both a rel and an attribute. And if we don't have two UAs supporting a given feature, it's unclear to me it should be in the spec.

Ping @zcorpan @sideshowbarker for your thoughts on this. I think we have two paths:

- Merge the PR as-is mostly, saying that rel=mask-icon and the color="" attribute do not have a processing model, but can be specified in valid documents. This follows the logic that processing models should not be specified for things without multi-vendor support.
- Add a processing model. This follows the logic that link rel=""s are special and can be added to the spec even without multi-vendor support. The precedent for this is theme-color (although I guess that might have Gecko support, just not implementation?).

I am personally OK with either, but I want us to be conscious of the tradeoff we are making.

> Merge the PR as-is mostly, saying that rel=mask-icon and the color="" attribute do not have a processing model, but can be specified in valid documents. This follows the logic that processing models should not be specified for things without multi-vendor support.

I think that would be the appropriate choice in this particular case. My rationale is:

* authors are using it intentionally (it’s not an unintended mistake—they don’t consider it an error)
* it doesn’t cause any known problems—e.g., no problems with security, performance, parsing or any other factors we normally consider when classifying something as an error
* it’s clear at this point that it’s not really important enough to anybody that  the processing model for this be defined in the HTML spec—nobody cares enough to take the time to do it, and the lack of it isn’t blocking implementations or causing real-world interoperability problems or anything else we’d normally consider when making it a priority to define in the spec

And of course a real-world positive effect of not continuing to block this on getting the processing model defined is that in the mean time the HTML checker can stop emitting errors for it.

The problem with the checker emitting errors about cases like this which authors don’t consider to be errors is that it risks causing authors to ignore other errors that are actually important, or to end up deciding the checker is irrelevant and just quit using it altogether.

Yep. To be clear, I think everyone wants to make sure that these are conformant, it's just a question of whether we specify the processing model at the same time. I don't think actually doing that would be that hard, if we just came to an agreement on it.

Let's wait a bit for @zcorpan or others to chime in but I'm happy to go ahead with merging this PR if you think conformant-but-no-processing model is best. (I haven't reviewed the actual patch recently; if it needs tweaking, I'll be happy to do it myself, as poor @XhmikosR was left hanging for so long already.)
@zcorpan: please check now.

We also need for this change to add `color` to the **Content attributes** section for the `link` element, right? And add `color` to the attribute index at the end of the spec. I chatted with @XhmikosR about it on IRC and reckon it’s probably better at this point for one of us to make those changes (along with deciding where to add mention about the reflecting IDL attribute for `color` being absent).

> We also need for this change to add color to the Content attributes section for the link element, right? And add color to the attribute index at the end of the spec.

I'm not sure, personally. I think it'd be fine to leave it out, since it's not a "real" attribute but instead one just allowed for validation. I guess we've never run into this kind of case before.
I guess it's kind of weird not to have it. Let me push a commit adding it, and everyone can let me know what they think.

> > We also need for this change to add color to the Content attributes section for the link element, right? And add color to the attribute index at the end of the spec.
>
> I guess it's kind of weird not to have it. Let me push a commit adding it, and everyone can let me know what they think.

Reviewed that commit and it all looks good to me—thanks
LGTM
Thanks, guys for all the help!
Mask icons and icons are completely separate features.
Thanks @domenic!
For others researching the possibility of using custom properties, i.e.  `<link rel="mask-icon" color="--my-color" ...>`, I opened a WebKit ticket https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=266440
